subject: nineTailedKitsune
pitch:
Category: Fantastical creature.
Subject: nine-tailed kitsune fox with spirit flames.
Style: high-fantasy anime.
reasoning:
I'm planning a nine-tailed fox design, standing on four legs facing forward, with fanned tails each ending in a spirit flame, and considering using the toon kit's glow effects for the design.

Now I'm working out the skeleton structure: hip and spine joints with catmull curve positions running from rump to chest, then neck and head joints branching off, plus a separate jaw joint. I'm setting up a body sweep along the spine chain with a radius function to shape the torso.

For the fur shading I'm using a cel-shaded furEdge material with cream belly countershading over orange, sweeping the neck with a tapering radius, and building the head as a scaled sphere with a muzzle, jaw, ear extrusions, and eye decals placed on the skull part.

Now I'm working out leg geometry with IK: front legs running from shoulder to foot with roughly equal upper/lower segment lengths, and hind legs with a digitigrade three-segment chain alternating knee and hock bend directions, setting hip and foot targets for positioning.

Now working out the nine fanning tails from the rump, each as a chain of base/mid/tip points with lateral spread angles and upward curvature to create a splayed tail arrangement.

Adding tail coloring and glow...

Adding forehead tomoe decal, a neck rope with paper shide zigzags and a gold magatama pendant on the chest, plus cheek spike tufts using cone spikes at the head sides. Now sizing the eyes relative to the skull sphere radius.

Positioning the head joint near the neck and defining a forward-facing muzzle frustum with a dark nose tip, then setting up the lower jaw joint and its own forward extrusion for the mouth piece.

For the jaw I'm adding tiny fang spikes jutting up, then shaping the ears as sharp-cornered triangular extrusions anchored at the sides of the head with some thickness.

Now I'm working out the inner ear geometry, offsetting it slightly forward so it pokes through the front face regardless of which side (left/right) the ear is on, and marking the tips black for contrast. Next I need to figure out where to place the eye decals so they're visible on the front of the sphere.

For textures, I'm planning around five: the anime eye, two colored flame SVGs with gradient layers (outer violet-blue, inner cyan, white core), and a face mark decal with a red crescent design placed on the forehead using a hit-test positioning approach.

Adding cheek stripe decals with mirrored SVG lines, handling null hit results safely, and working out the nine-tail arrangement attached to the hips with the base positioned to clear the body's rump geometry.

Now I'm figuring out foot placement using small flattened sphere paws sitting near ground level, then computing leg bend geometry for front and hind limbs — shoulder/hip anchor points, segment lengths, and bend directions needed for the two-segment front legs and three-segment hind legs.

For the leg sweeps, I'm choosing tapering radius arrays and a paint function that colors the lower leg as a dark sock versus the orange coat above, then starting on the body's sweep radius function with a slight sinusoidal variation.

For color, I'm deciding on a kitsune look with a golden-orange coat, white tail tips, and a furry textured edge transitioning to a cream belly.

Now I'm working out the head spikes for the cheek ruff, positioning them relative to the head bone with directional offsets, then planning a collar loop that sweeps around the neck surface.

For the neck loop, I'm placing it at the midpoint of the neck chain, giving it a thin red rope-like appearance, and distributing small gold bells and hanging paper cards evenly along it.

Now I'm setting up the skeletal rig: spine chain parented to hips with three named joints, neck chain parented to the spine tip, and a head joint parented to the end of the neck chain.

I'm plotting out the neck's curve points rising from the shoulders up to the head position, then sizing the head sphere and checking overall body proportions against a roughly 1.1m tall fox.

Now I'm building the skull geometry attached to the head bone with a scaled sphere, positioning the eyes symmetrically along the skull surface, and starting to set up flame card elements with frame orientations for the texture billboards.

For the flame, I'm deciding to anchor it at the tail tip bone, considering whether to orient it along the tail's tangent direction versus straight up — the tangent approach actually looks fine since the tail tip already points upward, so I'll build the frame from the tail tip position with an upward-facing orientation and bone rigidity.

I'm adding an orb glow at the tail tip using a small icosahedron with a white-blue glow effect, plus floating wisp cards scattered around the hips bone at smaller scale with their own glow applied. For the tail coloring, I'm setting up color bands transitioning from coat color to white near the tip, then working out the curvature math to fan the tail segments outward at increasing angles per segment.

For the fan shape itself, I'm computing each tail point's position by combining angle-based sine/cosine offsets with a lift factor that increases toward the center segments, building out three curve points per tail that arc backward and upward with the tip curling higher.

Tails max out at y=1.5 with z reaching -1.5, and I'm sizing the tail radii so adjacent tails overlap slightly at the base but stay separated enough at the tip. Now I'm adding haunch spheres at the hip joints for extra muscle bulk, naming each limb's joint chain consistently, and setting up color assignments per body part.

Working out the paw placement and sizing relative to the leg tip so it sits flush with the ground, then checking that the tail's spline points actually include a tip name since I only defined three spans with no explicit tip marker.

I need four names for the tail to give it a proper tip, using the last point as the flame attachment bone; front legs need three names (two spans) and hind legs four, then I'll write the final export.
